propositions: A test fixture's bare repository created with `git init --bare` at git defaults runs detached background maintenance after a push, which outlives the `subprocess.run()` call and continues mutating the object store concurrently with the immediately following `shutil.copytree`, causing the copy to fail with ENOENT on entries (maintenance.lock or fanout directories) being pruned mid-walk.

The race is not limited to lock files; fanout directories under objects/ vanish when maintenance repacks loose objects into packfiles during the copytree walk, making an `*.lock` ignore predicate insufficient.

Pinning `receive.autogc=false`, `gc.autoDetach=false`, and `maintenance.autoDetach=false` before any push into the fixture remote eliminates the concurrent mutator: the push spawns zero maintenance children and no background process remains when copytree begins.

A new guard test runs the push under `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` and asserts that no `git maintenance run` child carries `--detach`, with a positive control ensuring the trace recorded the push's receive-pack, so the guard cannot pass vacuously.

The existing test `test_copy_repoints_sibling_origin_and_keeps_refs_isolated` still proves its contract: a seeded defect that stops re-pointing the copied store to its own sibling origin causes the test's own assertion to fail, confirming the test is not weakened by the fix.
